title: Bypassing the Multimodal Tax: Hybrid RAG, SQL RRF & UI Telemetry - Abed Matini, Ogilvy
talk_summary: A demo-heavy walkthrough of a framework-free hybrid RAG FAQ chatbot (Docling→Markdown→Postgres pgvector + BM25, RRF ranking, Langfuse telemetry, tiny local Qwen 0.5B model). The transferable ideas are mostly about deterministic code over LLM agents, pre-LLM guardrails, and cheap small models when retrieval is clean.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic Python functions instead of LLM agents for tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Replaces agent loops with plain Python functions for things like date lookup and calculations, calling the LLM only once for the final natural-language answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if something can be done by a Python function, let's a Python function then run it for you

takeaways.technique: Pre-LLM guardrails in code, not prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Blocks disallowed queries (e.g. medical escalation, prompt injection) with intent regexes, term dictionaries and a classifier before anything reaches the model; system prompt stays tiny because rules live in code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the issue should stop before we um ... the prompt injection or anything that we have ... We shouldn't even send it to the LLM

takeaways.technique: Smallest capable model when retrieval/context is clean
takeaways.what_they_do: Downgraded from a 7B to a 0.5B Qwen instruct model after cleaning and structuring input data, claiming equal or better answers with less hallucination and lower latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need the biggest model. You if you can vet your data before sending it to your LLM, a smaller smallest model can sort you out

takeaways.what_they_do: Converts docs to Markdown with Docling and chunks by heading/paragraph/sentence rather than fixed 512-char windows, so each retrieved chunk is self-contained and traceable to a source.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of uploading uh straight uh 28 pages, we can if we can divide our documents to different chunks and just to different files, relevant files, and clean up that data

takeaways.technique: Rigid test suite for guardrails and deterministic paths
takeaways.what_they_do: Because guardrails and tool logic are code, they write tests asserting exactly what is blocked and why, rather than trusting an LLM to behave.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have rigid test and to say, "Okay, this is what I'm blocking and this is why." And it passes all the tests

takeaways.technique: Hybrid keyword+semantic retrieval with RRF ranking
takeaways.what_they_do: Combines BM25 exact-match with vector similarity and fuses ranks (RRF) so exact identifiers (SKUs, product names) aren't lost to semantic drift; tunes top-k per use case.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need the exact information ... we need to have both both basically uh keyword search and um and the semantic search together
takeaways.numbers: top-2 for FAQ; more for product catalogs
